name: Shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a smoky, spiced tomato and pepper sauce, scooped up with crusty bread.
story: Shakshuka is a staple across North Africa, particularly in Tunisia, Libya and Algeria, and is eaten from breakfast to light dinner. The name is often explained as meaning something like a mixture. It is traditionally cooked and served in the same pan, with bread for scooping.

steps.title: Soften the base
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide, deep frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Cook the onion and peppers for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and slightly browned at the edges.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.text: Add the garlic, tomato paste, harissa, cumin, paprika and caraway. Stir for 2 minutes until the paste darkens and the pan smells fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Pour in the tomatoes, salt and sugar. Simmer, uncovered, for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and jammy, with no watery liquid pooling.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Taste and adjust salt, harissa and sugar. The sauce must be well seasoned since the eggs will dilute it.

steps.title: Make wells
steps.text: Use the back of a spoon to make 6 to 8 hollows in the sauce. Crack an egg into each, season the whites lightly with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Poach the eggs
steps.text: Cover and cook on low heat for 5 to 8 minutes. The whites should be set and opaque while the yolks remain glossy and soft; cook longer for firm yolks.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Scatter over the herbs and bring the pan to the table. Serve straight from the pan with bread for scooping.

tips: Reduce the sauce well before adding the eggs, or they will sink and the whites will stay runny.
Keep the heat low once the eggs go in so the bases do not scorch.
Take care not to overcook; the eggs keep cooking in the hot pan after it comes off the heat.
Top with crumbled feta or merguez if you like.

swaps.swap: Use 1 tsp chilli flakes plus 1 tsp extra paprika and a little extra tomato paste.
Use 1 kg ripe fresh tomatoes, chopped, and cook a few minutes longer.
Leave out or use fennel seed for a hint of anise.
